item.title: Nollywood Stars Joke Silva, Funke Akindele, Others Pay Tribute To Pete Edochie
item.description: Nollywood stars Joke Silva, Funke Akindele, Mercy Johnson and others have paid tributes to veteran actor Pete Edochie, who died Wednesday after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer at the age of 79. The actor’s death was announced by his son, Chief Leo Pete Edochie, who confirmed that he died at 12:30 a.m. on November 25, 2026, in Enugu, Nigeria. His death has sparked an outpouring of tributes from colleagues, public leaders and entertainers who have celebrated his remarkable career, influence and legacy. Actress Joke Silva expressed sadness over his death, remembering his playful side. “Uncle Pete…I will miss your teasing. Rest well Sir,” she wrote. Filmmaker and actress Funke Akindele recalled growing up watching Edochie in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart , before eventually sharing the screen with him in the film Egg of Life . She expressed gratitude for his encouragement and the impact he made on younger generations of actors. “Thank you for paving the way for so many of us in Nollywood and for being an inspiration to us over the years. Your work lives on,” she wrote. Similarly, actress Uche Jombo described Edochie as one of Nollywood’s greatest pillars, a master of his craft and a custodian of Nigerian culture. She said the late actor “gave Nigerian storytelling a face, a voice and a legacy that will outlive generations.” “His contribution to Nollywood cannot be measured by the number of films he appeared in, but by the impact he made, the standards he set and the generations of actors he inspired.” Actress Omoni Oboli described his passing as the fall of an iroko tree, writing, “Hmmm 2026! It is well. The Iroko has fallen. Rest in power sir Pete Edochie.” May Edochie, the estranged wife of the late actor’s son, Yul Edochie, also paid tribute, describing him as an institution and a father figure to many. She reflected on the false reports of his death that had circulated over the years, noting that he had continued working despite the rumours. Actor Charles Inojie paid tribute using several of the late actor’s traditional praise names, including Ebube Dike, Ntu Mara Igwe and King of the Forests, before praying for his peaceful rest. While DJ Kaywise thanked him for his contributions to the industry, other entertainers who expressed their grief included comedian Sabinus, who described Edochie as an oracle and a legend. Pete Edochie was born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State. His ancestral roots, however, trace back to Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, in Anambra State. Edochie rose to prominence through his portrayal of Okonkwo in the 1987 Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart . His commanding screen presence, distinctive voice, and memorable delivery of traditional proverbs subsequently made him one of Nollywood’s most recognisable figures. Beyond his acting career, Edochie was also celebrated for his contributions to broadcasting and his influence on generations of Nigeri

item.title: Ebola Fight Runs Up Against Customs, Rites In Remote DR Congo
item.description: For health workers in the volatile eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), tackling local suspicions is as big a problem as combating the Ebola virus that has plagued it for six months. In the rural community of Bulambo-Isale, AFP saw a small crowd gather this week along a dirt track, determined to prevent an ambulance bringing the body of a local Ebola victim for burial. Victims of the highly contagious haemorrhagic fever, which spreads through direct contact with bodily fluids, must be interred in sealed body bags to prevent infection spreading from the corpse. Burial ceremonies are conducted by specially trained health workers, anonymous in protective hazmat suits, some of whom locals allege are brought in from outside the community and do not speak the local languages. In this file photo taken on March 09, 2019 Health workers are seen inside the ‘red zone’ of an Ebola treatment centre, which was attacked in the early hours of the morning in Butembo. – Democratic Republic of Congo’s government on June 25, 2020 officially declared an end to an epidemic of Ebola that broke out in the east of the troubled country in August 2018 and went on to claim 2,277 lives. (Photo by JOHN WESSELS / AFP) But custom dictates that the deceased be buried by their own family and their body be allowed to fuse with the earth of their ancestors. “The authorities have imposed the Ebola response on locals without first making sure how they interpret it,” grumbled Patricien Kambale, who became a livestock farmer after university. “The sick victim gets carted away in a vehicle and locals don’t know where they’re being taken. Then we learn later that the person has died so locals think the doctors are using poisoned medicine to kill people,” he said. Suspicions of ‘profiteering’ Health workers in Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) simulate with the help of an Outbreak Response Advisor admission protocols of suspected cases during a training by medical charity, Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) to reinforce regional emergency response capacity for Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo Locals say they are distrustful of Congolese authorities, who have a reputation for corruption and nepotism. Left to cope with the miseries inflicted by myriad armed groups that have stalked their mineral-rich region for more than three decades, they fear their customs and lives matter little to the powers that be. Wilson Kasyani, chief doctor for the Vuhovi health district that includes Bulambo-Isale, a rural settlement in North Kivu province, was worried for the ambulance and its occupants. “Weapons are everywhere” in the mountainous region, he said. Medical workers face almost daily attacks due to locals’ hostility to efforts to respond to the Ebola outbreak, which has killed more than 5,000 people out of more than 11,000 cases since May. “Today, people entered a nurse’s home and wounded her son,” Kasyani said wearily. “And yesterday we had to stop someone who wanted to attack invest

item.title: Barca, Real Madrid chief fail to reach agreement over ref scandal accusations
item.description: Real Madrid and Barcelona failed to reach an agreement on Wednesday in a conciliation hearing over statements made by Los Blancos president Florentino Perez regarding the Negreira refereeing scandal, a source from the Catalan club confirmed to AFP. The hearing followed a lawsuit filed by Barcelona on June 12 against Perez for his statements in May, in which he accused the Spanish champions of scheming to obtain favourable treatment from referees. “The aim of this lawsuit is for Mr. Perez to retract certain statements he made, knowing they were false, which are defamatory and offensive to the club’s image and reputation,” Barcelona had declared when initiating legal action. “In the event that this lawsuit is not duly addressed, Barcelona will proceed to file the corresponding criminal complaint for defamation,” Barca added in June. “When someone makes statements and you might be mistaken or go too far with your words, a conciliation hearing gives you the chance to correct them,” Barca president Joan Laporta told reporters before the hearing on Wednesday. “If that opportunity is not taken, it means we see malicious intent and we will have to continue with the proceedings.” Barca could now file a criminal complaint against Perez over his remarks. The main cause of the Catalan club’s anger was the press conference on May 12 in which Perez called elections for the Real Madrid presidency, which he later won. In that appearance he reiterated his accusations against Barca regarding the matter known as the “Negreira case”. Spanish courts are investigating alleged payments of around 7.5 million euros ($8.2m) made over almost two decades by Barcelona to companies belonging to Jose Maria Enriquez Negreira, the former number two in Spain’s refereeing hierarchy. The investigation seeks to determine whether those payments may have been used to obtain any competitive advantages, something Barcelona deny, claiming they were solely for reports analysing referees. item.title: NDC faults Yusuf over allegation against Kwankwaso
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in Kano State has faulted Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf over his allegation that he was pressured to facilitate discussions between the Presidency and Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso on a possible defection to the All Progressives Congress (APC). The party described the allegation as contradictory and unfortunate, claiming that it contradicted the Kano State Government’s earlier position on alleged negotiations with the Presidency. In a statement signed by its Chief Campaign Spokesperson, Hon. Hashimu Sulaiman Dungurawa, on Wednesday, the NDC said Yusuf’s recent interview with the BBC raised questions about his earlier comments on the matter. Yusuf had reportedly alleged that he was persuaded and pressured to facilitate discussions on behalf of Kwankwaso with the Presidency over a possible move to the APC. Reacting, the NDC recalled that the Kano State Government issued a statement on January 29, 2024, denying any deal, agreement or negotiation with the Presidency following the Supreme Court judgment on the governorship election. The party argued that the governor’s latest comments, coming about 34 months after the earlier statement, were inconsistent with the government’s position at the time. “The Governor’s 360-degree turnaround on the same subject after just 34 months, accusing Senator Kwankwaso, is to say the least contradictory, repulsive and unfortunate,” the statement said. The NDC further maintained that Yusuf’s decision to join the APC was a personal political choice and was not influenced by Kwankwaso. It also expressed concern that the allegation could embarrass the Presidency and undermine public confidence in the country’s political and judicial institutions. The party called on the Kano State Government to withdraw the allegation, particularly the part relating to Kwankwaso’s character. It added that statements allegedly made for political advantage or to attract public sympathy would not address the challenges confronting the governor’s administration. “Deliberate statements made to muddle things up for political gains and attract undue sympathy would not save an already sinking ship,” the party said. item.title: Baffi Furniture Celebrates 10th Anniversary, Unveils Luxury Plaza
item.description: Baffi Furniture, one of Nigeria’s prominent furniture and interior furnishing brands, celebrated its 10th anniversary alongside the grand opening of Baffi Luxury Plaza, marking a decade of growth, innovation and excellence. The event had His Royal Highness, Muhammadu Sanusi II, as the Chief Guest of Honour, alongside other distinguished guests, business leaders, industry stakeholders and valued customers who gathered to celebrate the company’s achievements. Established in 2016, Baffi Furniture has grown from humble beginnings into a household name in Nigeria and beyond, with showrooms across Abuja, Lagos, Kano, Enugu, Port Harcourt and Ghana. The unveiling of Baffi Luxury Plaza marked a significant milestone in the company’s expansion into the premium furniture market. The showroom features an extensive collection of luxury furniture, combining timeless elegance, innovative designs and exceptional craftsmanship. Under the leadership of its Chief Executive Officer, Bahtiyar Nalbant, Baffi Furniture has recorded significant growth over the past decade, driven by its commitment to quality, customer satisfaction and continuous innovation. The anniversary celebration also featured the recognition of long-serving employees in appreciation of their loyalty, dedication and valuable contributions to the company’s growth and success. As Baffi Furniture enters its second decade of operations, the company remains committed to raising industry standards, expanding its presence and redefining luxury living across Nigeria and beyond. item.title: NDLEA busts ₦303.9bn meth lab in Enugu, arrests Nigerian, five Mexicans
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — The National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) has dismantled an industrial-scale methamphetamine laboratory in Enugu State, arresting an alleged Nigerian drug baron and five Mexican nationals described as specialists in the production of the illicit drug. The agency said it recovered 1,512 kilogrammes of methamphetamine, valued at about $226.8 million (approximately ₦303.9 billion), from the facility, alongside 6.68 tonnes of precursor and essential chemicals and industrial equipment used in manufacturing the drug. The NDLEA identified the Nigerian suspect as 63-year-old Chuks Enoch Ezeike, popularly known as ‘Over Size’, while the five Mexican nationals were allegedly brought into the country to establish and operate the laboratory. Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the agency, Brig.-Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (retd.), disclosed the breakthrough at a media briefing at the NDLEA headquarters on Wednesday. Marwa described the operation as one of the agency’s most carefully planned intelligence-led operations, saying investigations traced the alleged drug network through Mexico, Colombia, France, the Republic of Benin, Lagos and Enugu. According to him, the agency’s Special Operations Unit began working on intelligence in April 2026, which identified Ezeike as a suspected specialist in establishing clandestine methamphetamine laboratories with alleged links to Oscar Ramos-Cardenas, a Mexican identified as a major industrial-scale methamphetamine producer. Marwa said the agency subsequently received intelligence on August 25, 2026, about five Mexican nationals identified as methamphetamine specialists travelling to Nigeria. He said the NDLEA, working with the Nigeria Immigration Service, prevented the five men from entering Nigeria when they arrived in Abuja on August 28 and returned them to Mexico. The NDLEA chairman said investigators later established that Ezeike had travelled from Enugu to Abuja to receive the visitors, with his bank records allegedly confirming payment for their hotel accommodation. Marwa said the suspects subsequently devised another route through Bogotá, Colombia, Paris, France, and the Republic of Benin. He alleged that Ezeike procured forged Argentine, Colombian and Chilean passports for the Mexican nationals, who surrendered their genuine travel documents and assumed new identities before entering Nigeria through the land border. According to him, three of the Mexicans entered Nigeria through the Seme Border Post on September 20, while the remaining two arrived the following day. The NDLEA boss said the agency deliberately allowed the suspects into the country to enable investigators to uncover the entire network, including the alleged financier, foreign specialists, laboratory and finished products. “We wanted the whole network: the meth specialist, the financier, the factory and the product. item.title: ‘Fix Edo roads or I won’t return’ – Benny Hinn tells Okpebholo
item.description: International evangelist, Pastor Benny Hinn, has urged Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, to urgently repair roads across the state, saying he would be reluctant to return if the poor road conditions persist. Hinn made the remarks in a video circulating on social media after his recent visit to Edo State, where he was hosted by Apostle Johnson Suleman, founder of Omega Fire Ministries International. The US-based televangelist disclosed that he met with Okpebholo during the visit and appealed to him to address the condition of roads he travelled on. “I went to Edo State and I met the governor. I just hope he fixes the roads. I don’t ever want to take that kind of bumpy road again,” Hinn said. “If they ever want me back in Edo State, the governor has to fix those bad roads,” he added. Hinn also expressed concern about a possible visit to Warri, Delta State, recalling the poor condition of roads he encountered during an earlier trip to the city. His comments come amid complaints by residents and motorists about deteriorating road infrastructure in parts of Edo State, with some routes reportedly affected by potholes and failed sections. One of the roads that has attracted complaints from commuters and transport operators is the Benin-Sapele-Warri highway, which links parts of Edo and Delta states. In September, the Edo State Government acknowledged the poor condition of several roads across the state, blaming some of the deterioration on what it described as poor-quality construction carried out under the previous administration. The government appealed to residents to be patient, promising extensive road rehabilitation during the dry season. Okpebholo also inspected some road and drainage projects in November and pledged to address the state’s infrastructure challenges. item.title: Kwara begins ₦2bn gratuity payments to 2018–2019 retirees, clears ₦7bn backlog
item.description: The Kwara State Local Government Staff Pension Board has commenced the payment of over ₦2 billion in outstanding gratuities to retired local government and Local Government Education Authority (LGEA) workers who left service between 2018 and 2019. The Chairman of the Local Government Service Commission and Local Government Staff Pension Board, Alhaji Umar Danladi Shero, disclosed this while briefing journalists on developments in the commission and efforts to address outstanding pension obligations. Shero said beneficiaries in the 2018–2019 retirement category had started receiving their payments following the completion of verification and screening exercises. He explained that the latest payment was part of the state government’s efforts to settle inherited gratuity liabilities and improve the welfare of retired local government and LGEA workers. According to him, the state government expended over ₦7 billion between July and October on gratuity payments to local government and LGEA retirees covering the 2011–2017 period. He said the ongoing disbursement of over ₦2 billion to the 2018–2019 beneficiaries represented a continuation of the exercise to clear outstanding gratuity obligations. The pension board chairman commended Governor AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq for his support and interventions in addressing the welfare concerns of retired workers at the local government, SUBEB and state levels. He said the governor’s interventions had supported regular pension payments and the gradual settlement of outstanding gratuities inherited from previous administrations. Shero assured pensioners that arrangements had been made to ensure a seamless and transparent payment process, adding that verified beneficiaries would receive their entitlements directly into their designated bank accounts. He reaffirmed the board’s commitment to ensuring that all eligible retirees received their entitlements, urging beneficiaries to remain patient and cooperate with the board where necessary. He added that the government remained committed to ensuring that no eligible pensioner was left out as efforts continued to clear outstanding gratuity liabilities. item.title: UCTH: Group presses for immediate CMD advert
item.description: …alleges plot to install acting head …Ikpeme dismisses claim as “falsehood” By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR A socio-political group, Good Governance Initiative (GGI), has accused the management of the University of Calabar Teaching Hospital (UCTH) of stalling the recruitment of a new Chief Medical Director (CMD), alleging a scheme to install an acting head and ease in a preferred successor. The Chief Medical Director, Prof. Ikpeme Ikpeme, has rejected the allegation. GGI’s Convener, Mr Bassey Okoi, made the demand in a statement in Calabar on Wednesday, calling for the immediate advertisement of the position, which falls vacant on April 16, 2027, when Ikpeme’s second tenure ends. Okoi said the vacancy should have been advertised in national newspapers six months before the incumbent’s tenure expires. The group had expected the process to start on November 1, he said, but there was no sign of it. He alleged that the delay was meant to tilt the succession in favour of a candidate from Cross River’s southern senatorial district. Okoi insisted that the central senatorial district should produce the next CMD under a long-standing zoning arrangement among the three senatorial districts. He recalled that Prof. Thomas Agan, from the northern district, served eight years before the office moved to the south. According to him, allowing the central district to produce the next CMD is the fairest course, and the incumbent appears determined to disrupt the arrangement. He stressed that zoning was not meant to undermine competence but to promote fairness, inclusiveness and a sense of belonging. He warned that manipulating the process could cause tension and damage institutional harmony. Okoi urged the Federal Ministry of Health to ensure that the recruitment was transparent, credible and consistent with regulations. He also appealed to stakeholders to back an equitable process, saying no individual or interest group should predetermine the outcome. When contacted, Prof. Ikpeme dismissed the claims and said he had already begun the process of appointing his successor ahead of time. He advised the group’s sponsors to stop wasting energy on what he called falsehood and to draw up a programme for taking the hospital to the next level instead. He said the group should take its concerns to the Federal Ministry of Health, the appropriate authority on such appointments. Pointing to the reforms he had carried out to reposition the hospital, Ikpeme said he was no party to the dispute. “I am not a contestant,” he said. item.title: Bayern confirm Musiala’s neurological symptoms began in 2025, pledge recovery support
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayern Munich and Jamal Musiala’s management have reaffirmed their support for the midfielder’s recovery and clarified that he was first examined for neurological symptoms on April 22, 2025, immediately after they appeared. In a joint statement after talks on Tuesday, the club and 11WINS, the agency representing Musiala, said: “Both sides agree that the player’s health comes first. Jamal Musiala has their full support on his road to recovery.” Addressing speculation about the midfielder’s health, they added: “Jamal Musiala was first examined for absence-like symptoms on April 22, 2025. This took place in consultation with FC Bayern and its medical department immediately after the neurological symptoms first appeared.” The statement said Bayern and Musiala’s management had agreed to continue discussions “in a spirit of partnership and confidentiality”. Musiala has said he was diagnosed with “easily treatable absence seizures, which are due to a neurological dysfunction” after collapsing twice in four days during pre-season. Bayern sporting director Max Eberl described Tuesday’s meeting as “very, very constructive” and said the club’s priority was helping Musiala return after a muscle injury sustained during the international break. “That’s the only task FC Bayern has currently, to give Jamal this trust and not some topics about money or something,” Eberl said. The talks follow debate over the Germany international’s form and his contract, which runs until 2030. Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen had questioned the lucrative extension if Musiala did not return to his best, while former chief executive Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested the deal might need to be renegotiated. Players’ union FIFPRO criticised the club’s public comments, saying an injury or dip in form was no reason to reopen agreed contract terms. Honorary president Uli Hoeness had said Musiala might never regain his previous performance level. Musiala has made five appearances this season, scoring twice. item.title: Ughelli Killings: Obidient Movement faults police, urges probe
item.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Obidient Movement has condemned the November 23 attack on the campaign team of former Deputy President of the Senate and Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) Delta Central Senatorial candidate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, in Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, which reportedly left four persons dead and several others injured. The movement expressed concern over the security situation in the state, accusing the Nigeria Police Force of failing to prevent attacks on political supporters and calling for an independent investigation into the conduct of officers deployed to the campaign ground. In a statement on Wednesday signed by its Director of Media and Communications, Onyeka Dike, the movement urged Nigerians to take their personal security seriously while calling on security agencies to ensure the protection of citizens irrespective of their political affiliations. It alleged that the police had failed to adequately protect opposition supporters during attacks in Delta State and accused some officers of showing bias in their handling of politically related incidents. The movement said it was particularly concerned that armed attackers reportedly operated at the campaign venue despite the presence of several truckloads of police personnel. The statement read, “The Obidient Movement strongly condemns the murderous attack on Senator Ovie Omo-Agege and members of his NDC campaign team in Uduere, Ughelli North, Delta State, by APC thugs on November 23, 2026, which left several people dead and others seriously injured, including outspoken activist, Comrade Efemena Umukoro (Akima) and Senator Omo-Agege’s aide, Comrade Moses Anuaghe.” The movement alleged that the attacks on NDC supporters in Delta State had continued despite the presence of security personnel. “We are particularly outraged by the conduct of the Nigeria Police Force during yesterday’s attack. Six truckloads of policemen were reportedly at the campaign ground, yet they failed to stop armed men from attacking and killing innocent Nigerians. What exactly were they deployed there to do?” it queried. It also cited Omo-Agege’s reported suspicion that the policemen deployed to the venue were not there to protect him but to supervise an attempt on his life. The movement further alleged that the same security personnel had previously taken a different approach when NDC supporters confronted an attacker during an earlier incident. It also cited allegations by the Omo-Agege campaign organisation identifying Ughelli North Local Government Chairman, Jaro Egbo, as the leader of the attackers, and called for an investigation into the allegation. The movement claimed that political violence in the state was not an isolated development, recalling an earlier incident in which an AK-47 rifle was reportedly recovered from a suspected political thug. item.title: Malaysia Sues Google For $146m Over YouTube Content
item.description: Malaysia said Wednesday it was suing Google for $146 million over the tech giant’s failure to remove “harmful” content posted on video-sharing platform YouTube. “The lawsuits concern two separate matters involving Google’s alleged failure to comply with its statutory obligations and applicable licence conditions,” the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission said. The first suit related to the US firm’s alleged failure to take action against “thousands of online materials including gambling, scams and fraud”, the watchdog said in a statement. The MCMC said it had submitted 73,703 reports to YouTube between January 1 and October 28 this year, the majority of which related to online gambling. In this file photo taken on June 28, 2013 a webcam is positioned in front of YouTube’s logo in Paris. (Photo by LIONEL BONAVENTURE / AFP) Of these gambling-related reports, some 4,950 cases received no response, while a further 35 cases took more than 90 days for a platform response or takedown, the MCMC added. A further 1,468 cases exceeded 30 days from the date of submission, it added. “These figures demonstrate the scale of harmful content on the platform and the delays in addressing such content,” the watchdog said. The second case related to YouTube’s failure to take down alleged defamatory and false content posted by a Malaysian blogger after the MCMC received a complaint. Google could not immediately be reached for comment. The lawsuits came three weeks after Google announced plans to invest $15 billion in Malaysia over the next two years to build data centres and other infrastructure, expanding on a $2 billion investment announced in 2024. The country is Southeast Asia’s fastest-growing hub for new data centres crammed with servers that can train and run AI tools such as chatbots and image generators. Malaysia had previously taken other major social media platforms, including TikTok, to task over allegations that they had failed to remove content deemed “grossly offensive”.
